brief.scope: Security feasibility only: independently verify the supplied Codex 0.153.4 hook failure/coverage/context findings against matching official source. Assess enforceable alternatives outside the incomplete hook path: native tool/permission restrictions, host mediation or a bounded vendor correction. Identify whether complete pre-effect decisions, safe credential separation, no human approval fallback and native harness UI can coexist. Study the external harness mechanisms, not approval of our GPT-6-authored implementation. Keep canonical execution, no writable production MCP, no alternate executor and permanent dev/prod separation. Read-only official network research is authorized; no model launches, code edits, parser writes, credentials, settings/state/admission or bypass flags. Return evidence-backed security requirements, reachable options and exact unknowns; no full implementation plan. Actual model is Daybreak; do not self-credit GPT-5.

findings.claim: The required fail-closed pre-effect decision cannot be enforced through Codex 0.153.4 PreToolUse hooks. Matching handlers fail open on execution errors, malformed or unsupported responses, most nonzero exits, and serialization failures; the runtime then continues execution.
findings.reproduce: Official matching source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.4/codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs#L179-L302 and https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.153.4/codex-rs/core/src/hook_runtime.rs#L175-L215. Tests explicitly name unsupported decisions and invalid allow responses as fail-open.

findings.claim: PreToolUse lacks complete effectful-tool coverage and execution-context binding. write_stdin and code-mode wait return no payload, outer code-mode execution uses a Custom payload ignored by the default handler, and exec_command supplies only the command while resolved workdir and environment identity are absent. Consequently the adapter cannot prove every surface was intercepted or bind a decision to the actual executable context.

A command hook is not a safe credential boundary. Codex snapshots its parent environment at session creation and replays it into hook subprocesses; shell-tool environment policy and sandbox permissions do not contain those hook processes. Using an untrusted hook as the admission gate can therefore expose harness credentials independently of tool sandboxing.

envelope.note: Daybreak security feasibility conclusion: stock Codex 0.153.4 hooks cannot satisfy the declared admission contract. Native filesystem/network permissions, approval_policy=never, closed shell-environment inheritance, disabled unnecessary tools and read-only MCP provide a useful coarse containment baseline with no human fallback, but not complete semantic pre-effect decisions. A potentially reachable host-mediated option is the same Codex app-server with no command allow rules, deterministic handling of command/file approvals, raw effects denied by native containment, and only a bounded host capability invoking the existing canonical dispatcher; the native remote TUI can remain the UI. This option must preserve separate dev/prod profiles and expose no writable production MCP. It is not yet admissible because exact 0.153.4 behavior remains unverified for absent/disconnected approval responses, comprehensive stdin review, suppression of every non-mediated effectful built-in, and ownership of approval messages when the native remote TUI is connected. The other reachable option is a pinned bounded vendor correction that makes required policy failures fail closed, covers or disables every effectful route, supplies resolved cwd/environment/executable context, and runs the policy helper with sanitized credential custody. Complete pre-effect decisions, credential separation, no human approval fallback and native UI can therefore coexist conditionally through proven host mediation or that vendor correction, but not through the current hook path or native configuration alone.
